scope.required_core_interface_exception: Ordinary adopt cannot validate a prospective design through _load_design because that function first reads the live current-design.json. A partial retry also cannot call current bind_inputs on its coherent old basis while live publication is inconsistent. Propose one shared validation extraction plus a keyword-only explicit validated-basis mode on bind_inputs, detailed below. No schema or gate change. These exact state.py seams require explicit review/parent authorization and affected C1 revalidation before editing frozen code.

evidence.inference: A supported recovery producer is a prerequisite, not an adapter to attach after immutable null-identity admissions. Defer those new records and predicates entirely. An ordinary v1 CLI remains useful if its adoption entry path is explicitly specified.
evidence.qualification_blocker: No available qualified producer supplies pre-admission identity plus complete lifetime/guard-inactivity evidence. Stop that path; no alternate platform search is authorized.

history.archive_policy: Exact r1 byte copies, not corrected historical prose. Relative links in the archived HTML retain their original bytes; use the current overview for navigation.

F1.change: Withdraw C2R-D-first recovery state/gate implementation, all v2 ownership records, resolved recovery dataclasses/qualifier signatures, lifetime predicates and second acquisition-lock protocol. No latent production interfaces or dead tests for an unavailable positive.
F1.dispatch: Only C2b-ordinary-v1 can proceed after final review. It never resolves an interrupted executable lifetime.

F2.change: No upgrade_ledger, archived v1 ledger, mixed-prefix validator or new version. Existing persistent v1 inputs retain ordinary semantics. Preserve historical artifacts. Specify only ordinary initial/revised adoption publication using existing v1 schemas and the finite table below.
F2.bound: Retained ordinary candidate workflow/design documents support exact publication retry; they are not a ledger archive, migration, second event journal or mutable status tracker.

F3.change: Unknown spawn blocks all currently unsupported recovery. No current exception. A future qualified complete-environment-reset path could resolve it only with qualified pre-admission environment/guard binding and inactive pending launch authority. That is a deferred constraint, not an executable interface.

F4.change: No numeric review wall-clock guarantee. Resolve unchanged exact reviewed/report bytes and subject-bound metadata before the accepted append; ledger sequence establishes acceptance order. Do not use mtime or invent a FindingResult timestamp.
F4.future: Real platform capture/guard/lifetime temporal qualification remains mandatory before any future recovery, separate from review-byte acceptance.

ordinary_boundary.cli_options: Retain design-contracts.json.cli.workflow options for status/next/record/close/adopt exactly. No new flags, command overrides or bypasses. recover is absent from accepted subcommands; invoking it yields argparse's unsupported-command exit 2, not a pretend recovery result.
ordinary_boundary.help_and_operator_guide: List five actually implemented verbs once implemented. Explicit limitations section: original recover is deferred/blocked; unresolved executable lifetime stops mutation/dispatch in this workspace. No age, PID, direct/root exit, deleted lock, new directory/worktree, imported report or automatic replay clears it. Human approval remains unconfirmed unless actual attributed evidence exists. Installing a tool or making a clean worktree is not a reset.
ordinary_boundary.normal_load: status/next/record/close use load_workspace and bind_inputs; no alternate permissive loader. status may report malformed/incomplete adoption, not readiness to dispatch. Only adopt has the narrow raw-read publication entry below.
ordinary_boundary.lock: Use one CLI lexical lock at .ai\SLUG\evidence\workflow.lock via the existing evidence.exclusive_lock for every mutating operation, held through revalidation and writes and, for next, capture/completion. Original LockOwner metadata in this lexical file is collision ownership only, not durable recovery authority. No extra acquisition lock is needed because no stale lock is released. A present/orphan lock gives conflict 3; never delete or steal it.
ordinary_boundary.admission: Under that lock, load/bind/evaluate; blocked implies no runner call. Persist v1 admission and launch-intent before run_capture, then synchronous actual observer events. No authority is hidden in reason, receipt_refs, another tracker, or synthetic process events. A command/handoff follows the original registered definition only.
ordinary_boundary.uncertain_lifetime: No completed event on observer-persistence failure or unresolved launch/capture state, even if callback later saw direct exit or wrapper returned zero. Preserve actual observations, error diagnostics and unresolved admission. CLI preflight rejects every mutating path with RECOVERY_UNVERIFIED obtained from authoritative Readiness; it does not remove/filter admissions. Read-only status remains available.
ordinary_boundary.normal_completion: For an ordinary observed terminal capture without recovery uncertainty, retain existing completion rules and child/structured outcome separation. launch-failed has the observer's actual null returncode, not an invented child 127; the wrapper still returns its actual 127/125. Failed/no-spawn is not executed work. Timeout/cleanup uncertainty is not repaired from a root exit. Do not retrofit these CLI classifications onto old completed ledger records.
ordinary_boundary.handoff: Null-command check admissions await response; no child/launch intent and no process-recovery interpretation. record accepts only the matching admitted attributed proof under unchanged receipt validation. Existing pending handoffs and completed history remain intact across ordinary compatible adoption.
ordinary_boundary.record_close: Preserve the original immutable receipt/producer/current-source/prerequisite checks. Review/report bytes must resolve before acceptance append; ledger sequence, not invented review timestamps, binds order. close must check actual resolved Git commit/current feature HEAD and scoped committed source/modes/membership against the proven source, not just accept a 40-hex string. Gate readiness/mandatory verification/review/metrics remain required. No fake positive quality closure while Q2-Q5 proof is absent.
ordinary_boundary.lifetime_preflight_for_adopt: On a coherent old state, evaluate the existing ship target with its bound inputs and resolved ledger; refuse RECOVERY_UNVERIFIED without requiring ship's ordinary closure proofs to be complete. This consults Readiness, not a copied lifetime state machine. In a partial revised retry use bind_inputs(root,W0,ship,design=P0,ledger=L0) and ResolvedLedger(L0,resolve_receipts(root,slug,L0,claim_receipt_ids)), then the unchanged evaluate. No copied unresolved predicate or private _Evaluation(None) shortcut. The retry cannot append a lifecycle resolution or permit a child.
ordinary_boundary.scope_observation: Lock/output paths must not accidentally be input evidence. Retain current _snapshot_for exact-output exclusion restrictions; do not add a broad .ai exclusion or weaken snapshots to hide these files. Choose declared input scopes that do not cover the transient lock. An incompatible scope is an explicit input/design error, not silently normalized away.

adopt_contract.purpose: Initial and revised v1 design adoption only. No recovery, migration, historical execution import or general transaction-repair API.
inputs_without_new_flags: --revision REV selects retained .ai\SLUG\design-history\REV.html and .ai\SLUG\contracts\REV.json as already required by _load_design.

Also stage .ai\SLUG\design-history\REV.workflow.json (existing WorkflowContract shape) and REV.current-design.json (existing CurrentDesign shape). These are immutable proposed publication documents, not new record schemas.

--review PATH is a safe repository-relative JSON file containing the existing DesignReview metadata shape, exactly equal as a value to candidate CurrentDesign.review. Its artifact points to the unchanged independently produced report. Its candidate_hashes must bind document/components/canonical WorkflowContract exactly; copy no reviewer identity to the adopter.

All staged candidate files, metadata/report/dispositions/authorization and retained history refs are read/hash-checked before writes. Missing or malformed candidate input is error 2. No CLI-generated approval, revision or claimed historical execution.

For revision adoption, retain exact current workflow.json and current-design.json bytes as design-history\OLD.workflow.json and OLD.current-design.json before appending the new adoption. If identical retained files already exist, reuse them. If any existing retained file differs, including a partial earlier write, conflict 3 with no overwrite. This retains ordinary design inputs, not the ledger.

For candidates published by this CLI, workflow/current-design JSON serialization is the existing write_json_atomic sorted UTF-8 JSON plus LF. Retained proposed JSON documents must use those canonical bytes so retry comparisons are exact. Older coherent v1 live documents may be noncanonical; retain their original bytes for the old-side comparison, without rewriting history.

new_shared_validation_seam.signature: validate_design_binding(root: Path, contract: dict, design: dict, ledger: dict) -> dict
new_shared_validation_seam.what: Validate explicit contract/ledger shapes and slug agreement, then the same design schema, retained paths/artifacts, review/context/unattended authorization, candidate hashes, normative components, history/adoption order and source bindings currently in _load_design. Return the validated design. Read-only; no adoption, append, repair, gate invocation or weakening of checks.
new_shared_validation_seam.as_is_to_be: _load_design(root, contract, ledger) still reads only current-design.json, then delegates to this helper. load_workspace retains its signature; bind_inputs retains existing positional-call behavior with the explicit paired keyword extension below. Both normal paths remain fail-closed. The helper permits adopt to validate an in-memory prospective triple before any live publication, or the exact pre-append basis on retry.
new_shared_validation_seam.callers: Existing _load_design, explicit-basis bind_inputs mode, and planned workflow.py adopt path only. No caller-supplied validation callback, temporary permissive live state or isolated fake workspace.
new_shared_validation_seam.why: AC04/05/09: one reusable validation body plus the paired explicit-basis binding mode prevent bootstrap/retry deadlocks without duplicating design or lifetime policy. These are narrow read-only state seams, not a general loader redesign.

explicit_basis_binding.signature: bind_inputs(root: Path, contract: dict, target: dict, *, design: dict | None = None, ledger: dict | None = None) -> ResolvedInputs
explicit_basis_binding.rules: Existing three-positional-argument behavior remains unchanged. Both optional values must be supplied together or neither; one alone raises ValueError. If both are supplied, validate the exact contract/design/ledger triple through validate_design_binding, then reuse the existing dependency_closure/_snapshot_for materialization loop unchanged. Do not read the inconsistent live pointer in this branch. No fabricated snapshot or omitted target scopes.
explicit_basis_binding.caller_boundary: Only adopt's A1/A2 old-basis validation uses explicit values; ordinary status/next/record/close must use normal load/bind. This makes the existing pure evaluate usable for authoritative lifetime preflight against the exact historical prefix without duplicating its predicate. No historical prefix becomes dispatch permission.

new_shared_validation_seam.proof_reopened: C1 _load_design/load_workspace/bind_inputs design-validation, snapshot-scope parity and history/artifact/approval mismatch tests plus prospective-empty-basis/partial-publication cases. Gate, record schemas, runner and evidence.py remain unchanged. If another core change is needed, stop with the exact seam; do not expand these two read-only state interface changes.

terminology.W0_P0: Exact previous canonical-location workflow/current-design bytes, retained under their old revision paths and verified as a coherent old state. For initial bootstrap both are absent.
terminology.W1_P1: Exact staged candidate workflow/current-design bytes for REV; both existing v1 shapes, canonical serialization.
terminology.L0: Actual valid v1 ledger immediately before a new adoption, expected_seq=n. It stays on disk unchanged until append. For initial bootstrap only, it is the existing-schema empty ledger.
terminology.E: Exactly one ordinary v1 adopted event for REV at n+1, no admission/process/receipt/closure. On retry read E from the actual ledger rather than regenerate its run_id/time.
terminology.L1: L0 plus E. In a partial publication retry E must be the final event; later runtime events in an incoherent publication are a conflict.
terminology.candidate_validation: Validate prospective (W1,P1,L1) using validate_design_binding before append. Validate old (W0,P0,L0) for revised adoption, including its exact current source/artifact bindings. Initial basis has no old design and must be truly empty authority, not a discarded prior ledger.

event_construction: Use the existing Event fields: kind=adopted, target=REV, fresh unique run_id, receipt_refs=[], outcome=ready, process=null, child_exit=null, spawned=no, completion_commit=null, actual append UTC time and diagnostic reason. Producer identifies the self-declared acting designer/adopter, never the independent review producer. No new fields.

Event.inputs.source is a real source_snapshot of the immutable candidate HTML/normative/workflow/current-design documents, exact --review metadata, review report/dispositions/authorization, retained history refs and, on revised adoption, retained exact W0/P0 files. Store ordinary GuardSnapshot only. Check all expected byte hashes, not filename presence.

Event.inputs.contract has adopted_contract_sha256=canonical_hash(W1), components=P1.components, actions={}, checks={}, claims={}. This is design provenance, not guarded execution proof. Validate snapshot, event at n+1 and prospective ledger using existing validators.

Re-read exact candidate bytes and live basis under the lock immediately before append_event(workspace,E-without-seq,n). If hashes/sequence changed, no append. F4 guarantee is exact reviewed bytes resolved before accepted sequence, not numeric reviewer time.

After append, publish workflow.json first, current-design.json second, using write_json_atomic. Finally load_workspace must succeed on the published candidate. No child executes during publication. Do not report adoption success before this final coherent load.
initial_bootstrap: adopt is dispatched before any unconditional load_workspace call. Acquire the same lexical mutation lock and raw-read only the named authority/candidate files with safe_path/read_json and strict validators.

A fresh bootstrap requires both live workflow/current-design absent, candidate history=[] and supersedes=null, and ledger absent or exactly empty v1 ledger for this slug. No existing adopted/lifecycle event may be discarded or inferred away.

Missing authority is not evidence of process separation. Refuse bootstrap if this workspace is known to have unresolved prior guard execution or remnants contradict an empty basis. Do not reinitialize a damaged existing ledger. Untracked hostile deletion is outside this cooperative trust boundary, not a supported reset.

When ledger is absent, exclusively initialize only the empty existing v1 shape, flush/fsync and validate it; do not overwrite an existing file. A partial/malformed initialization conflicts and stops. No historical admission, receipt or approval is imported.

Construct E and validate the full prospective triple without reading a live pointer; append through existing append_event once the empty ledger exists. Then publish W1, then P1. An unwound interruption after empty initialization is the B1 table row, not a call to the failing normal loader.

finite_publication_retry_table.disk: Every other combination: P1 before W1, mismatched bytes/review/hash/slug/history, missing old retained input after E, partial immutable file, malformed ledger, E not final while publication incoherent, revision duplicate/different candidate, newer adoption or lost authority
finite_publication_retry_table.checks: No guessing from mtime, reason, PID, lock age, a partial file or candidate existence
finite_publication_retry_table.action: Stop: input error 2 for malformed input; conflict 3 for inconsistent publication. No overwrite, rollback, duplicate append, lifecycle repair, child or new design loop

retry_limits: The table describes adopt-only publication retry after exception unwinding releases the owned lock. A process death leaving a lexical lock blocks entry with exit 3. No automatic stale-lock repair or universal crash-recovery claim.

Before E, exact orphan retained candidate/old-design copies confer no authority; A0/B0/B1 may reuse them only after validating all candidate/current inputs. Partially created immutable copies are conflicts, never silently truncated or replaced.
All revisions/IDs and candidate paths are validated before I/O. Files not named by current/candidate history are not searched for a replacement state. No mutable transaction/status file is added.

A1/A2 cannot invoke normal load first. They raw-read the finite named inputs, validate the exact old and prospective triples through the shared helper, and use the ledger's actual E/prefix. After publication they must call normal load.

On a partial revised retry, unresolved executable lifetime is tested against the validated L0 prefix and the old contract without deleting any event from the actual ledger. Reconstruct only that historical validation basis, not a filtered dispatch ledger. No next/record/close can use this basis.

Prospective adoption must preserve action/check/increment IDs referenced by existing runtime events and the executable-versus-null-command classification for admitted actions. Do not turn an unresolved executable admission into a handoff, remove it or reinterpret it via adoption. Compatible component/command changes reopen proof by existing freshness rules; incompatible historical ID retirement stops for a later contract decision.
